stem: Silicon melts at a much higher temperature than phosphorus. Which explanation correctly identifies the structures and attractions overcome? Enter 1, 2 or 3. (1) Silicon has a giant covalent lattice and melting breaks strong Si–Si covalent bonds; phosphorus consists of P₄ molecules and melting overcomes weaker instantaneous dipole–induced dipole attractions between molecules, leaving P–P bonds intact. (2) Both elements consist of simple molecules, but silicon has stronger intermolecular attractions. (3) Melting phosphorus breaks P–P covalent bonds, while melting silicon only overcomes intermolecular attractions.
